rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a conceptual learning and problem-solving plan. It begins with the meaning and procedure of the product rule, using one complete example before guided work. The following short sessions reduce support and finish with independent mixed application. Sessions fit the available 15-minute windows.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build the product rule from a worked example and connect each term to its source.
sessions.amountLabel: One rule and one complete worked example
contentTargets: The formula (fg)' = f'g + fg'
How the two terms arise when differentiating a product
completionEvidence: Explain what changes and what stays unchanged in each term of the product rule
Apply the rule to one product using the worked example as a guide

sessions.title: Apply the Rule Step by Step
sessions.objective: Use the product rule on polynomial products with limited guidance.
contentTargets: Selecting f, g, f', and g'
Substituting correctly into the product-rule formula
completionEvidence: Solve one derivative with step prompts
Solve one similar derivative without step prompts

sessions.title: Recognize When the Rule Applies
sessions.objective: Distinguish products from expressions requiring only the power rule, then differentiate correctly.
contentTargets: Recognizing products of functions
Choosing between the product rule and the power rule
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by the rule they require
Solve one product-rule derivative and simplify the result

sessions.title: Independent Product Rule Check
sessions.objective: Demonstrate independent use of the product rule and repair any error found.
sessions.amountLabel: Two independent derivatives and one error check
contentTargets: Independent setup and differentiation
Checking signs, terms, and simplification
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule without a prompt
Solve two product-rule derivatives independently

items.essentialIdea: The product rule states (fg)' equals f'g plus fg'.

check.title: State the product rule
check.prompt: What is the derivative of the product fg?
check.referenceAnswer: (fg)' = f'g + fg'. It adds the derivative of f times g and f times the derivative of g.
check.feedback: Both factors contribute one term; do not collapse them into one derivative.

items.essentialIdea: Differentiating a product gives one term from f and one term from g.

check.title: Where product terms come from
check.prompt: Why does differentiating fg produce two terms?
check.referenceAnswer: Because each factor can vary while the other is held unchanged, giving f'g and fg'.
check.feedback: The two terms come from changing each factor separately, not from repeating the same derivative twice.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the product rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which rule correctly differentiates a product fg?
recognitionCheck.feedback: The correct rule has two terms, one for each factor.
